To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hexapeptidic probe (HVGGSSS) binds to the cell surface of tumor cells that respond to ionizing radiation.
the TIP-1 protein is a molecular target of the HVGGGSV peptide, which is a promising molecular probe to predict tumor response to ionizing radiation.

a hexapeptidic probe, HVGGSSV, can be used as a molecular probe to detect TIP-1, a protein translocated to the plasma membrane of cancer cells after exposure to radiation and that the translocated TIP-1 may serve as a biomarker to predict the tumor response to radiotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel molecular probes and imaging techniques for the noninvasive and quantitative evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy in the clinic.
a novel approach to molecular imaging of tumor response to radiation therapy.
the development of a molecular imaging probe for the assessment of tumor response to radiation therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HVGGSSVS is a molecular imaging probe for TIP-1 and that TIP-1 is a molecular biomarker of radiation response in tumors and cancer cells.
the TIP-1 peptide binding is a biomarker of the tumor response to IR treatment.
the HVGGSSVs peptide and TIP-1 are promising molecular targets for the in vivo imaging of the tumor response to radiation therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HVGGSSVs and its antibody may have potential to be developed into a novel molecular imaging probe to monitor the tumor response to IR and/or other treatments.

we have identified a molecular biomarker (TIP- 1) that is a target for molecular imaging of tumor responsiveness to IR treatment and that a molecular imaging probe (HVGGSS) can be used for the in vivo imaging of the biomarker.

the radiation-inducibility of the TIP-1 cell surface relocation is associated with the enhanced tumor cell susceptibility to the subsequent radiotherapy and thus can be used as an early biomarker to predict tumor response to the prescribed radiotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TIP-1 may be used to develop a new class of molecular probes to monitor tumor response to IR treatment and thus tailor radiotherapies.
the TIP-1 peptide can be used to predict radiation response of tumors and that this peptide may have potential as a biomarker for radiation response.

the TIP-1 is a molecular target of the radiation-inducing peptide (HVGGSSVS), and the peptide binding to TIP-1 can be used as a molecular imaging biomarker for predicting the tumor responsiveness to IR.
